title: Weekend A La Carte (November 21)
summary: 40 great films for Christian parents to watch with their kids / Does the body really keep the score? / There’s no such thing as “your” weekend / To efficiency and beyond / What happens when schools ban phones / GTA 6 is pornographic and gory See Also Weekend A La Carte (December 27) Weekend A La Carte (November 30) Weekend A La Carte (May 25)
content: Good morning and welcome to Weekend A La Carte. Be sure to scroll down to read this week’s Reader Recommendations, since you will find some good and interesting ones there. And check in again tomorrow for Works & Wonders. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include some superb books like Kevin DeYoung’s Daily Doctrine and Mark Vroegop’s Waiting Isn’t a Waste . I have updated the Commentaries on Sale page. It includes deals in both print and Kindle editions, and you’ll find some great discounts there. Recommended Reading Brett McCracken watches a lot of movies, and that gives him the authority to create this list of 40 great films for parents to watch with their kids. In today’s glutted, morally compromised streaming-media environment, Christian families are right to worry about the countless options billed as “kid-friendly” but actually form kids in spiritually unhealthy ways. As a dad of four young kids, I know the struggle well. It’s impossible to keep up with the content conveyor belt of new film and TV options being marketed to kids. Christian parents need trusted curators who can reliably point us to entertainment that isn’t just “safe” for our kids to watch but is actively promoting laudable themes and (sometimes accidentally) modeling Christian virtue. This list is my attempt to help my fellow Christian parents in this struggle. The movies below are all G- or PG-rated and generally “safe for the whole family,” though parents should still consult online content guides to discern the appropriateness for their particular family. Read: 40 Great Films for Christian Parents to Watch With Their Kids. You’ve no doubt heard something about Bessel van der Kolk’s The Body Keeps the Score , a book that has been on the bestseller charts for more than 10 years. That book has done more than anything else to normalize a particular understanding of the relationship of the body to the mind and of the body’s response to trauma. Matthew Loftus, author of Resisting Therapy Culture explains why van der Kolk’s explanation is unsatisfying and no longer credible. As important as arguments over how to interpret scientific research are, the larger problem with pop theories of trauma has to do with misapplications of that research and outright misinformation. You may have seen ads, videos, or blog posts proclaiming that procrastination is a trauma response, a statement with no basis in scientific research but still accepted easily because it’s far easier to let go of one’s guilt over procrastination if it’s linked to trauma. The Canadian physician Gabor Maté argues that most mental illness is somehow linked to trauma—another baseless assertion that is nonetheless very popular. Expanding the definition of trauma can be powerful because it gives people a story that explains how they got to where they are—regardless of whether or not that story is true. We can’t always draw a hard-and-fast line to say “ this is psychological trauma” while “ that is just a very stressful experience” because stress and trauma are more of a continuum than two distinct categories. However, what we see now is an attempt to maximize the number of things considered as trauma, even using the language of “microtrauma.” Read: Does the Body Really Keep the Score? Since we have come to the weekend, perhaps you’d do well to be challenged by Zak Mellgren who wants you to know that it’s not “your” weekend. “How was your weekend?” I’ve used this phrases countless times myself. It is an ingrained, deeply rooted piece of my vocabulary. A conversation starter. A way to communicate interest in another person’s life. And let’s be clear up front, that is a wonderful thing. It is good to ask another image bearer about their daily life. “How was your weekend” opens the door to countless possible avenues of conversation. We will often get surface level small-talk from this question, but even these little details are worth our time. And we might get more than small-talk. We may learn of a doct

title: Teach Your Children About Those Who Were Sent
summary: It was a great honor to be able to partner with Missionary to create Goers, a series of illustrated biographies for children. Each biography introduces young readers and listeners to the stories of men and women who were sent by churches to spread the good news about Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. See Also A Gift Guide for the Christian Reader on Your List Releasing Today: Eric’s Greatest Race John Calvin (Christian Biographies for Young Readers)
content: It was a great honor to be able to partner with Missionary to create Goers , a series of illustrated biographies for children. Each biography introduces young readers and listeners to the stories of men and women who were sent by churches to spread the good news about Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. Each is illustrated by the ultra-talented Rommel Ruiz. The books can be purchased as a set of three or as individual volumes. The Plowboy’s Bible: The Story of William Tyndale’s English Translation . Hunted by spies, William Tyndale fled across Europe with a bounty on his head, his Bible translation labeled as contraband. Young John, on the other hand, has a long day of farm work ahead of him. Although their lives seem worlds apart, John’s father knows a story that binds John and William together—their love for God’s word. The scripture John relies on for encouragement cost William everything, but they gave John’s family everything! Rescued from Darkness: Amy Carmichael and the Girls of Dohnavur . Kumari is scared, helpless, and alone in a dark temple until Amma, a mysterious woman from a faraway land, carries her away to a beautiful garden. This is not a fairy tale. It’s the true story of missionary Amy Carmichael and the children she rescued and raised at Dohnavur Fellowship in India. Into the Unknown: David Livingstone’s Heart for Africa . Before David Livingstone was the most famous man in the world, he was a boy who dreamed of being free to explore God’s creation. But when David reached the mission field, he found that freedom taken from the people he tried to teach about the Creator. This is the story of a goer’s dangerous journey to the ends of the earth, of his courageous stand for justice, and of his patient endurance for the sake of Christ. The Goers series is written for children ages 4–10, and is ideal for parents to read to their children or for young readers to read on their own. Each book includes discussion questions and prayer points to get your family thinking and praying about the Great Commission. Each hardcover volume has 40 full-color pages and is sized 10″ x 10″. The Goers series is currently available exclusively through Westminster Books . Look for three more volumes to be added to the series around this time next year. summary_zh: 在告别之际，她没有忘记最重要的东西。11 月 24 日星期一，在波多黎各首都圣胡安的最后一次登台亮相中，法蒂玛·博施（Fátima Bosch）留下了令人难忘的最后一幕。这位墨西哥佳丽在2025年环球小姐加冕典礼上高举一条白色绶带，上面写着“Viva Cristo Rey”（基督为王万岁），结束了她为期一年的任期。这是她延续自己从未中断的信仰见证的一种方式。
title_zh: “基督为王万岁！”：环球小姐的告别
content: Au moment de tirer sa révérence, elle n’a pas oublié l’essentiel. Lors de son dernier passage sur scène, lundi 24 novembre, à San Juan, capitale de Porto Rico, Fátima Bosch a offert une dernière image marquante. Couronnée Miss Univers 2025, la Mexicaine a porté haut une écharpe blanche sur laquelle était inscrit « Viva Cristo Rey » (Vive le Christ-Roi), au terme de son année de règne. Une manière de prolonger un témoignage de foi qu’elle n’a jamais cherché à dissimuler. Ce dernier défilé s’est déroulé lors de la 75e édition du concours Miss Univers. Vêtue d’une robe bleu ciel scintillante, coiffée de sa couronne et visiblement émue, la jeune femme a tenu la bande au-dessus d’elle, laissant apparaître ces trois mots qui l’accompagnent depuis son sacre. Une façon de refermer cette parenthèse internationale en rendant hommage à Celui qui, selon elle, a guidé son parcours. Au moment de faire ses adieux, Fátima Bosch a également livré quelques mots sur le sens Tout lire… The post « Vive le Christ-Roi ! » : les adieux de Miss Univers appeared first on Aleteia .

summary_zh: 教宗方济各在公开接见活动中呼吁基督徒发出“向世上掌权者发出的呐喊，这呐喊源自人民的苦难、被杀害和致残的儿童以及支离破碎的家庭”。11月25日星期三，教宗恢复了专门讲解梵蒂冈第二届大公会议文件的教理讲授系列，重点阐述了《教会在现代世界牧职宪章》（Gaudium et spes）中关于促进和平的内容。在聚集的数千名信徒面前，

content: Les chrétiens doivent lancer un « cri qui monte vers les puissants de ce monde, porté par la souffrance des peuples, des enfants tués et mutilés, et des familles détruites », a lancé Léon XIV lors de l’audience générale. Ce mercredi 25 novembre, le Pape a repris son cycle de catéchèses consacré aux documents du Concile Vatican II, en s’arrêtant sur la promotion de la paix dans la constitution Gaudium et spes.  Devant les milliers de fidèles réunis place Saint-Pierre malgré une météo maussade, le souverain pontife a rappelé que « la paix n’est jamais chose acquise une fois pour toutes, mais sans cesse à construire ». Loin de toute vision naïve, le Concile Vatican II, vingt ans après la Seconde Guerre mondiale et en pleine guerre froide, avait déjà Tout lire… The post Suffit-il de prier pour la paix? summary_zh: 在一个政治派别水火不容的国家，一位电影人竟然能够同时赢得《人道报》、《星期日报》、《泰勒拉玛》和《费加罗报》的青睐，这真是一个好消息。这是因为他的电影并不将孩子们及其父母视为需要灌输思想的脑袋，而是视为需要唤醒心灵、激发惊叹的个体吗？在皮克斯工作过一段时间并参与了两部《阿斯泰利克斯历险记》动画片的制作后，路易·克利希（Louis Clichy）通过
title_zh: 《紧身胸衣》或低头的优雅
content: Bonne nouvelle au pays des camps politiques irréconciliables, un cinéaste peut enthousiasmer à la fois l’Humanité, le JDD, Télérama et le Figaro. Est-ce parce que son film ne prend pas les enfants, et leurs parents, pour des cerveaux à endoctriner, mais pour des esprits à éveiller et des regards à émerveiller ? Après un passage chez Pixar et des collaborations pour deux Astérix d’animation, Louis Clichy donne sa pleine mesure personnelle avec le Corset, le plus beau dessin animé que nous ayons vu depuis longtemps. Seul le souvenir de la larme qui tombe lentement sur la joue de Grincheux devant le cadavre de la Blanche-Neige de Disney nous semble à la hauteur de l’émotion ressentie ici. Dessin animé, disons-nous, plutôt que film d’animation, pour rendre hommage aux traits à l’encre de Chine et aux couleurs d’aquarelle, qui reposent l’œil des perpétuelles stimulations numériques. Le modèle de ce bijou visuel n’est manifestement pas l’esthétique de jeu vidéo. Qu’on ne compte pas non Tout lire… The post « Le Corset » ou la grâce de la tête penchée appeared first on Aleteia .

title_zh: 凯撒·阿尤布（Qaiser Ayub）因“亵渎”罪被判处死刑
content: L’affaire n’est pas sans rappeler celle d’Asia Bibi. Qaiser Ayub, marié, père de trois enfants, se trouve actuellement dans le couloir de la mort alors que la Cour suprême du Pakistan a confirmé sa condamnation pour « blasphème ». Ce chrétien pakistanais est déjà détenu depuis plus de 12 ans. Le 7 octobre, la plus haute institution judiciaire du Pakistan a confirmé son exécution au titre de l’article 295-C du Code pénal, qui prévoit cette peine en cas de propos jugés blasphématoires contre le prophète Mahomet. En 2010, un homme dénonce auprès de la police un blog (alors inactif) qu’il a lu et sur lequel il affirme avoir vu des textes offensant l’islam, textes pourtant non présentés par la Cour. Deux frères sont arrêtés en 2014 avant d’être tous deux condamnés, quatre ans plus tard, à la peine de mort : Qaiser et Amoon. Ce dernier est finalement acquitté et libéré plusieurs années plus tard, faute de preuves suffisantes contre lui. Et Tout lire… The post Qaiser Ayub, condamné à mort pour « blasphème » appeared first on Aleteia .

title: Kehilangan yang Membawa Berkah
title_zh: 带来祝福的失去
content: Oleh: Gevonny Dinda Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Gevonny Dinda, biasa dipanggil Dinda. Sebagai orang Kristen, saya merasa bersyukur dilahirkan di dunia ini dan berkesempatan untuk mengenal Tuhan Yesus. Saya sungguh bahagia dapat merasakan berkat-Nya setiap hari dan sangat bersyukur akan apa yang Tuhan Yesus berikan kepada saya selama ini. Kabar baik, kabar buruk, cobaan, dan berkat, saya terima dengan penuh rasa ucapan syukur. Di sini, saya akan menceritakan salah satu berkat Tuhan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada 19 Februari 2015, saya menerima kabar buruk bahwa kakek saya telah berpulang ke rumah Tuhan. Kepergian kakek saya sangat membekas di hati banyak orang, terutama nenek saya. Nenek saya sangat merasa kehilangan karena memang nenek belum siap menghadapi hal ini sehingga membuat kondisi badannya melemah. Sejak ditinggal kakek, kondisi mental dan fisik nenek saya semakin memburuk. Awalnya, ia merasa sangat kesepian dan merasa takut jika ditinggal sendirian di rumah. Bahkan, nenek saya sering menangis jika merasa kesepian. Ibu saya dan ketujuh saudara kandungnya akhirnya sepakat untuk bergantian menjaga nenek saya di rumahnya supaya tidak merasa kesepian lagi. Setelah itu, hari-hari nenek saya berjalan normal seperti biasa. Namun, karena umurnya yang bertambah tua, kondisi fisiknya semakin melemah. Sejak 2017, nenek saya sudah tidak kuat lagi berjalan dan harus memakai kursi roda. Di situlah, ketabahan dan kesabaran anak-anaknya, termasuk ibu saya, diuji dalam mengurus nenek saya. Pakde, budhe, tante, dan om saya yang hidup di luar kota, seperti: Jakarta, Yogyakarta, dan Kudus, semakin sering menyempatkan diri pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bergiliran mengurus nenek saya. Sampai pada April 2018 lalu, kondisi nenek saya berada di titik terburuknya. Karena anak-anaknya sudah memiliki firasat yang tidak baik, mereka memutuskan untuk berkunjung bersama-sama ke rumah nenek saya. Mereka hanya bisa berdoa bersama untuk kondisi ibu mereka. Sampai pada akhirnya, Tuhan Yesus memanggil nenek saya untuk ikut bersama-Nya. Karena sudah siap dengan kepergian nenek saya, kami semua menerima kepergian nenek dengan sukacita dan penuh ucapan syukur karena nenek saya sudah sembuh dan pergi ke tempat yang lebih indah, menyusul kakek saya. Tidak disangka, kepergian kakek dan nenek saya membawa berkah bagi keluarga besar kami. Tuhan Yesus memiliki kuasa untuk membuat keluarga kami menjadi lebih dekat satu sama lain. Hubungan anak-anak beserta cucu-cucu mereka menjadi lebih dekat. Kakak-kakak Ibu saya yang dahulu sering pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bertemu dan menjenguk orang tua mereka, sekarang lebih menghargai waktu kebersamaan dengan keluarga yang diberikan oleh Tuhan. Sejak saat itu, kami semua memiliki satu grup chat dan sering menanyakan kabar satu sama lain. Bahkan, kami semua memiliki keinginan untuk lebih sering bertemu pada masa depan, dan melakukan kegiatan bersama-sama seperti berlibur dan arisan keluarga. Semua itu tidak pernah terjadi sebelum kepergian kakek dan nenek saya, dan saya sungguh percaya Tuhan Yesus turut campur tangan dalam semua kejadian yang menimpa keluarga saya. Ia tidak pernah berhenti untuk menunjukkan betapa sayangnya Ia terhadap anak-anak-Nya, bahkan ketika anak-anak-Nya sedang berada dalam keterpurukan. Tuhan Yesus selalu memiliki rencana yang indah untuk setiap anak-anak-Nya, dan saya sangat percaya Ia telah memberikan sesuatu yang besar untuk membalas rasa kehilangan keluarga saya selama ini. Tuhan Yesus memang sungguh baik! Semoga Tuhan selalu memberkati keluarga Anda!

title: Berbagi dengan Mengajar dan Melayani
title_zh: 通过教学和侍奉来分享
content: Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Zefanya. Saya bersyukur karena pada kesempatan ini, saya dapat menyaksikan cinta kasih Tuhan yang Ia nyatakan melalui kegiatan mengajar bahasa Inggris yang saya lakukan secara volunter untuk anak-anak di beberapa desa di sekitar kota Salatiga. Kegiatan yang diselenggarakan oleh salah satu yayasan Kristen yang bergerak di bidang pelayanan dan pendidikan ini dilakukan setiap hari minggu. Pada kesempatan itu, saya beserta teman kuliah dan satu staf dari yayasan mendapat tugas untuk mengajar anak-anak di sebuah desa yang letaknya cukup jauh dari kota Salatiga, tempat kami tinggal. Butuh waktu sekitar dua jam lebih untuk sampai ke sana. Selama perjalanan, medan yang dilalui cukup sulit karena kami harus melewati jalanan aspal yang telah rusak parah dan jalanan tanah yang cukup sempit. Kami juga harus bersahabat dengan hawa panas yang sangat menyengat akibat dari teriknya sinar matahari ditambah dengan banyaknya tanah tandus dan pohon kering di sepanjang perjalanan. Namun, hal tersebut tidak mengurangi semangat kami untuk bertemu dengan anak-anak yang akan kami ajar. Setelah melalui perjalanan yang cukup melelahkan, akhirnya kami tiba di salah satu rumah warga yang akan kami gunakan untuk kegiatan belajar mengajar. Beberapa anak telah berkumpul di dalam rumah itu dan ketika mereka melihat kedatangan kami, mereka langsung membentuk barisan memanjang dan satu per satu mulai memberikan salam kepada kami. Alangkah manisnya! Saya sangat kagum dengan sikap mereka yang sangat ramah yang dapat membuat siapa saja ingin tersenyum ketika melihat mereka. Saya mulai mengajak mereka bercerita tentang pelajaran mereka di sekolah. Ada sekitar dua puluh anak yang datang untuk belajar. Usia mereka bervariasi, dari usia TK hingga SMP. Melalui percakapan mereka, saya mengetahui bahwa sebagian besar dari mereka belum pernah diajarkan bahasa Inggris di sekolah. Anak-anak SMP pun belum mengetahui pelajaran bahasa Inggris tingkat dasar seperti berhitung dari satu hingga sepuluh, atau menulis kosakata sederhana lainnya. Mereka juga bercerita tentang harapan mereka ke depan untuk memiliki fasilitas belajar yang memadai dan memperoleh lebih banyak kesempatan lagi untuk belajar bahasa Inggris. Hal itulah yang membuat kami sadar betapa mereka sangat ingin belajar hal-hal baru, tetapi fasilitas yang ada masih jauh dari kata memadai. Saya pun bersyukur karena dari kegiatan ini, mereka mendapat kesempatan untuk mempelajari hal-hal baru tersebut. Waktu belajar dimulai. Kami mengawalinya dengan berdoa, dan sebagian besar dari mereka, yang berbeda keyakinan, ikut melipat tangan dan menutup mata mereka. Selesai berdoa, kami membagi mereka dalam kelompok kelas kecil dan kelas besar. Kelas kecil terdiri dari anak usia TK hingga kelas tiga SD, sedangkan kelas besar terdiri dari anak-anak kelas empat SD ke atas. Saya mendapat kesempatan untuk mengajar anak-anak kelas besar. Banyak hal yang saya coba ajarkan kepada mereka, mulai dari kosakata sederhana tentang binatang, mengerjakan soal, hingga bermain gim sederhana untuk mengasah kemampuan bahasa Inggris mereka. Rasa lelah dan capai tentu kami rasakan karena mengajar anak-anak seusia mereka bukanlah perkara yang mudah. Namun, pada saat seperti itulah, kami menyadari bahwa kegiatan tersebut kami lakukan untuk memuliakan nama Tuhan. Kami yakin dan percaya bahwa Tuhanlah yang akan memberi kekuatan yang membuat kami mampu untuk melakukannya dengan baik. Kegiatan hari itupun selesai. Kami bersyukur bahwa kegiatan mengajar itu dapat kami lakukan dengan cukup baik terlepas dari kekurangan dan kendala yang kami rasakan sewaktu mengajar. Semangat belajar dari anak-anak juga membuat kami terdorong untuk memberikan pengajaran yang lebih baik lagi pada masa yang akan datang. Kami sangat bersyukur karena Tuhan memberikan perlindungan dan kasih-Nya kepada anak-anak yang kami ajar sehingga mereka masih dapat bertumbuh dengan baik dan memperoleh kesempatan-kesempatan untuk mengembangkan pengetahuan mereka. title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

title: Kembali Kepada Jalan Tuhan
title_zh: 回归主的道路
content: Nama saya Yoel, saya adalah seorang mahasiswa semester terakhir dari salah satu universitas swasta di Jawa Tengah. Saya dilahirkan dalam keluarga Kristen. Ibu dan Bapak saya cukup baik dalam membimbing saya untuk tetap dalam jalan Tuhan. Penyertaan Tuhan itu baik dalam kehidupan saya. Baiklah, saya akan ceritakan apa dosa yang sudah pernah saya lakukan. Rokok, pornografi, dan buang-buang waktu adalah keseharian saya pada waktu saya duduk di bangku SMU. Pada waktu itu, saya merasa ada yang kosong dalam hidup saya, tepatnya tidak ada gairah untuk mencapai suatu tujuan. Saya tidak merencanakan masa depan, pokoknya hidup terus mengalir. Sebenarnya, saya tertarik dengan dunia perfilman, saya ingin menjadi sutradara, tetapi ayah saya tidak mengizinkannya karena dia tidak melihat ada bakat seni dalam diri saya. Menurutnya, orang seni hanya akan mendapat uang atau pengakuan jika karyanya diterima. Kalau tidak mendapat pengakuan, ya "habis". Itulah perkataan ayah saya, saya masih ingat jelas. Menurut saya, dosa itu nikmat. Namun, saya juga sadar bahwa itu hanya kenikmatan sesaat. Saat saya masih SMU kelas satu, selama setahun saya merokok, tetapi saya benar-benar tidak dapat merasakan kenikmatannya. Mungkin itu hanya alat bagi saya supaya diterima oleh teman-teman saya. Saya suka mencoba hal baru, mungkin itu juga motivasi saya saat itu. Namun, jangan salah paham, teman-teman saya tidak pernah memaksa saya ikut merokok. Akhirnya, saya berhenti merokok saat kelas dua. Sebelumnya, sejak SMP kelas tiga, saya sudah kecanduan pornografi. Video porno begitu menarik bagi saya. Keinginan untuk melihat adegan dewasa itu sangat kuat. Ketika kuliah, pada tahun kedua, saya mulai berusaha serius untuk menghentikan kebiasaan tersebut. Saya mulai berpikir tentang dampak buruk pornografi secara serius. Menurut saya, sepertinya hanya saya yang ingin benar-benar lepas dari pornografi dalam lingkup pertemanan saya. Teman-teman saya sepertinya menerima hal itu sebagai sesuatu yang normal. Saya pun juga berusaha menerimanya sebagai sesuatu yang normal, tetapi saya tidak bisa berpikir seperti itu. Pasti ada dampak buruknya, saya yakin itu. Salah satu dampak buruk yang sudah saya rasakan adalah rendah diri. Saya selalu merasa diri saya itu "sampah". Dampak lainya adalah ketika saya melihat lawan jenis, saya akan cenderung menjadikannya objek seks. Itu sungguh menghancurkan martabat manusia sebagai makhluk yang berakal budi. Saya merasa kalau saya menonton video porno dan onani (ini sangat umum dalam dunia remaja), Tuhan akan membenci saya dan tidak menganggap saya lagi. Saya pernah berpikir untuk meninggalkan Tuhan dan hidup sesuka hati saya. Suatu saat, pernah saya berpikir bahwa saya sudah terlalu berdosa sehingga tidak bisa diperbaiki. Namun, Yesaya 1:18 menyadarkan saya bahwa Tuhan selalu menerima pertobatan manusia, tidak peduli seberapa buruk dosa yang sudah dilakukannya. Dalam kelemahan saya, Tuhan seolah-olah berkata, "Tidak apa-apa, Nak, bangun dan jangan berhenti." Pada tahun ketiga kuliah saya, sebenarnya saya sudah bisa lepas dari pornografi, dalam arti tidak kecanduan, tetapi tetap ada satu atau dua kali saya tergoda. Saya juga mengisi beberapa tahun dalam hidup saya kecanduan gim (game). Saat SMP, gim PS2 membuat saya menghabiskan uang jajan saya. Saat SMU dan kuliah, gim komputer membuat saya lupa waktu. Memang gim ini menjadi suatu pelampiasan akan rasa rendah diri saya. Selain bermain gim, aktivitas lain yang saya kerjakan adalah makan dan mandi. Saya tidak peduli akan hal lain. Tentu saja, sekarang saya menyesal, berapa banyak waktu yang saya buang. Alangkah baiknya jika dahulu saya melakukan sesuatu yang produktif, seperti mengasah kemampuan dalam bidang tertentu. Menyia-nyiakan waktu yang diberikan Tuhan adalah dosa, karena hidup kita menjadi tidak berguna. Saya juga pernah berjudi daring. title: Pertolongan yang Tidak Pernah Terlambat
title_zh: 永远不会迟到的帮助
content: Oleh: Odysius B. Temara Bersyukur untuk kasih karunia Tuhan yang selama ini tidak henti-hentinya saya rasakan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada kesempatan kali ini, saya ingin berbagi tentang kisah pengalaman hidup saya. Semasa kuliah, saya merasa bahwa saya adalah salah satu orang yang paling beruntung karena hampir selalu mendapatkan kemudahan dalam studi saya. Saya mendapatkan dosen-dosen yang ramah, teman-teman yang selalu mendukung saya, bahkan para staf akademik yang sangat bisa diajak bekerja sama. Semuanya berjalan sesuai dengan apa yang saya rancangkan sampai tiba-tiba segalanya berubah ketika saya menginjak semester akhir. Saya sangat terkejut ketika mengetahui bahwa saya diberi dosen pembimbing yang terkenal sangat sulit untuk penulisan skripsi saya. Beliau adalah salah satu dosen yang paling sibuk dan paling susah untuk dihubungi, terlebih untuk konsultasi. Pernah sampai tiga minggu beliau keluar kota, sakit, dan terlalu sibuk dengan tugas-tugas mengajar sehingga skripsi saya menjadi terbengkalai karena saya tidak bisa berkonsultasi dengan beliau. Ketika saya sedang berkonsultasi dengan beliau, sering kali beliau juga menyelipkan kalimat-kalimat sarkastik yang terkadang membuat saya lebih tertekan lagi. Seiring berjalannya waktu, teman-teman saya mulai lulus satu per satu, dan saya masih terjebak. Pada saat itu, saya merasa sangat kesal karena skripsi saya tidak kunjung selesai. Bukan karena saya yang malas-malasan, tetapi karena sulitnya menemui dosen pembimbing saya. Saya sempat mempertimbangkan untuk pindah pembimbing, tetapi rasanya sangat sayang kalau harus mulai dari awal lagi. Saya menceritakan keluh kesah saya kepada orang tua saya. Ayah saya menyarankan saya untuk lebih giat lagi berdoa, serahkan semuanya kepada Tuhan. Saya berdoa kepada Tuhan supaya Dia melembutkan hati dosen pembimbing saya dan juga memberi kekuatan dan kesabaran untuk saya dalam menghadapi beliau. Hari demi hari, saya berdoa dan sedikit demi sedikit tampak mulai terjadi perubahan pada sikap dosen pembimbing saya. Perubahan sikap itu tidak hanya terjadi kepada saya, tetapi juga kepada anak bimbingannya yang lain. Akhirnya, dengan proses yang cukup panjang, saya berhasil menyelesaikan skripsi saya dan lulus pada 12 Agustus 2014. Meskipun rancangan saya gagal untuk bisa lulus dalam 3,5 tahun, saya merasa bersyukur karena pertolongan Tuhan tidak pernah terlambat bagi saya sehingga saya masih bisa lulus tepat waktu. Sampai sekarang, saya senantiasa mengucap syukur kepada Tuhan atas segala yang Tuhan izinkan terjadi dalam kehidupan saya. Saya menyadari bahwa seberat apa pun permasalahan hidup yang saya hadapi, tangan kuat Tuhan akan selalu ada untuk menuntun saya melewatinya.

title: Merasakan Kasih Natal
title_zh: 感受圣诞节的爱
content: Natal merupakan liburan yang paling istimewa bagi ayah saya. Persiapan menjelang Natal, berbelanja hadiah, dan menghias rumah tidak membuatnya lelah - bahkan ia sangat menikmatinya. Ibu bercerita, ayah memperkenalkan saya dengan pohon Natal saya yang pertama waktu saya masih berusia sembilan hari. Pohon Natal itu kecil, tetapi setiap hiasan, lilin, dan untaian perada perak digantungnya dengan sangat teliti pada tempatnya, seolah-olah hanya ia yang dapat melakukannya. Setelah selesai, ayah mengangkat saya dari keranjang buaian dan menggendong saya supaya melihat hasil pekerjaan tangannya. Ayah masih menghias empat pohon Natal sesudah itu dan setiap kali pohonnya lebih besar dari tahun sebelumnya. Pada hari ia meninggal -- tak lama setelah menderita radang paru-paru -- ibu duduk dengan saya membicarakan Natal. "Madeline," katanya lembut, "Sinterklas akan memberikan hadiah untukmu, tetapi kita tidak mempunyai pohon dan hiasannya. Tahun ini pengeluaran kita sudah terlalu banyak." Besok hari Natal, tetapi sampai pagi ini tidak ada persiapan khusus untuk keesokah harinya, selain kebaktian pagi dan makan malam di rumah salah seorang anggota keluarga. Menjelang sore, telepon berbunyi dan ibu mengangkatnya. Tidak lama kemudian saya mendengar ibu berkata, "Anda baik sekali, tetapi rasanya kami akan melewatkan malam Natal di rumah. Natal ini pertama kali sejak ..." Lalu ibu dapat melanjutkan lagi, berterima kasih kepada penelepon itu sekali lagi dan menutup pembicaraan. "Siapa Bu?" tanya saya. "Salah seorang tetangga kita," kata ibu. "Ia mengundang kita malam ini. Ibu ... Ibu tidak bisa." Ibu diam saja hampir sepanjang hari. Sorenya, ibu berubah pendapat. Ia menelepon tetangga kami, mengatakan kami akan mampir sebentar. "Dia baik sekali," kata ibu kepada saya, "dan kita tidak mau dianggap tidak menghargainya." Setelah kami membunyikan bel pintu rumah tetangga kami, nyonya rumah menyambut dan mencium kami, lalu mengantar kami melewati serambi. Ruang tamu kelihatannya gelap, tetapi anehnya ada cahaya yang berwarna-warni. Ia mengajak kami masuk, dan saya melangkah ke dalam ruangan dan terperangah. Di sana, di tengah taburan lampu yang berwarna-warni dan bermacam-macam hiasan, lengkap dengan hadiah-hadiah yang dibungkus dengan kertas wama-warni yang cerah, berdiri sebuah pohon Natal yang indah sekali. Di sekeliling pohon itu duduk Ny. Abrams, Ny. Cohen, Ny. Blount, Ny. Dreyfus, sambil tersenyum lebar. "Selamat datang!" sapa mereka serempak. Sampai sekarang saya dapat memejamkan mata dan mengingat kisah tersebut dengan jelas. Sering ingatan itu menguatkan saya apabila keadaan memburuk, waktu saya meragukan hati manusia. Saya masih dapat merasakan kasih tetangga kami -- kaum ibu Yahudi yang mengambil risiko untuk melaksanakan tradisi yang tidak mereka kenal supaya seorang anak Kristen yang sudah tidak mempunyai ayah tetap dapat bergembira merayakan Natal. - Madeline Weatherford | Dipublikasikan | : | http://natal.sabda.org |

title: México abre un año de memoria y reconciliación a cien años de la Cristiada – Infovaticana Blogs
summary: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo
content: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo 22 de noviembre el Año Jubilar por el centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. La celebración comenzará en la solemnidad de Jesucristo, Rey del Universo, y se prolongará hasta el 21 de noviembre de 2027. El Jubileo lleva como lema “Su fe, nuestra memoria y su testimonio, nuestra misión”. Su propósito no consiste únicamente en recordar los acontecimientos que sacudieron la vida religiosa del país entre 1926 y 1929, sino en recuperar el testimonio de los mártires, promover la reconciliación y reafirmar la libertad religiosa como un derecho de toda persona. La presentación del emblema oficial, presidido por la proclamación “¡Viva Cristo Rey!”, ofrece una síntesis visual de esa finalidad. El diseño adopta la forma de un medallón o relicario en cuyo interior aparecen la Iglesia y el pueblo congregados bajo Cristo Rey. La Virgen de Guadalupe, la Eucaristía radiante, las coronas real y de espinas, así como las figuras del clero, la vida consagrada, los jóvenes y los fieles laicos, articulan una composición construida alrededor de tres conceptos: fe, memoria y testimonio. El color guinda remite a la sangre derramada por los mártires y las estrellas evocan el manto de la Virgen de Guadalupe. El emblema, por tanto, no constituye solamente la identificación gráfica de una efeméride, pretende expresar la continuidad histórica de una experiencia religiosa y transmitirla a las generaciones que conocen la cristiada como un episodio cada vez más distante. El Año Jubilar fue anunciado el 9 de noviembre durante la misa de apertura de la CXXI Asamblea Plenaria de la Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano, celebrada en la Basílica de Guadalupe. En ese contexto, el obispo de Cuernavaca y presidente de la CEM, Ramón Castro, subrayó que recordar la persecución religiosa no significa reabrir heridas, alimentar resentimientos ni señalar enemigos. La memoria cristiana de la resistencia cristera, explicó el Episcopado, debe conducir al reconocimiento del sufrimiento, la reconciliación y la construcción de la paz. Esta precisión resulta indispensable para evitar que el centenario sea utilizado como exaltación de la violencia o como argumento para trasladar al presente las confrontaciones políticas y religiosas del pasado. El Jubileo cuenta con un decreto de la Penitenciaría Apostólica, fechado el 6 de noviembre de 2026, mediante el cual se concede indulgencia plenaria a los fieles que cumplan las condiciones establecidas por la Iglesia y peregrinen a los santuarios dedicados a los mártires mexicanos o a los templos jubilares designados por los obispos. La Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano pidió que el decreto sea proclamado en las Iglesias particulares este 22 de noviembre y que cada diócesis disponga los lugares, celebraciones y actividades pastorales correspondientes. La apertura nacional comienza así a adquirir características propias en las comunidades diocesanas. Entre las convocatorias más amplias se encuentra la del arzobispo de Guadalajara, cardenal José Francisco Robles Ortega. El prelado convocó a toda la Iglesia que peregrina en esa arquidiócesis a celebrar el Jubileo del centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. El documento señala que la solemnidad de Cristo Rey de este año coincide con la celebración de los beatos mártires mexicanos, el Día del Laico y la Jornada Mundial de la Juventud. Sin embargo, sostiene que la fecha adquiere una profundidad particular por cumplirse cien años del comienzo de la resistencia. La arquidiócesis de Guadalajara propone vivir el Jubileo como una experiencia de comunión eclesial, memoria agradecida y renovación de la fe. La convocatoria recuerda a quienes permanecieron fieles a Jesucristo y a la Iglesia hasta entregar su vida y reafirma el derecho del pueblo a celebrar, transmitir y vivir su fe tant

Dal «fallimento salutare» che lo storico individua nel 7 ottobre alle fratture che attraversano oggi la società israeliana, l’intervista ripercorre la promessa del sionismo, la sovranità e la vulnerabilità ebraiche, l’accusa di colonialismo, il riemergere dell’odio antiebraico e il suo rapporto personale con la Francia. Al termine di questo lungo colloquio, Bensoussan formula una distinzione significativa: esprime fiducia nel futuro del sionismo, che concepisce come un processo di emancipazione dell’essere ebreo non conclusosi con la nascita dello Stato, ma considera più preoccupante la questione della stessa sopravvivenza dello Stato d’Israele, minacciata, a suo giudizio, innanzitutto dalle proprie fratture interne. Un’intervista approfondita, senza eludere le questioni più difficili, riletta integralmente dall’avvocato Michel Laval. Lei conclude ‘Una nuova storia del sionismo’ nel 1950. Se dovesse scrivere oggi il capitolo che inizia il 7 ottobre 2023, quale titolo gli darebbe? Senza alcuno spirito di sterile provocazione, lo intitolerei «un fallimento salutare», perché, come dopo il trauma della guerra del Kippur, esattamente cinquant’anni prima, il massacro genocidario del 7 ottobre 2023 ha indotto la società israeliana a interrogarsi su una certa arroganza, a rimettersi in discussione, dopo aver sottovalutato il nemico e sopravvalutato se stessa. È dallo shock seguito al Kippur del 1973, e naturalmente dalle trasformazioni della società israeliana, che è nata la svolta del 1977, quando per la prima volta l’opposizione di destra è arrivata al potere. Il suo libro racconta come un popolo vissuto in una condizione di dipendenza politica abbia deciso di tornare a essere soggetto della propria storia. Il 7 ottobre ha rivelato che la sovranità ebraica non aveva eliminato la vulnerabilità degli ebrei? La sovranità ebraica rappresentata dal sionismo politico non ha mai preteso di abolire la vulnerabilità degli ebrei. La sovranità dà vita a una nazione israeliana che non ha nulla a che vedere con il concetto di comunità ebraica. In altre parole, lo Stato d’Israele è uno Stato-nazione, non una comunità ebraica in più. L’assalto alla nave Altalena, nel giugno 1948, sulle spiagge di Tel Aviv, ne è un esempio. Ben Gurion ordina di sparare con i cannoni contro il mercantile noleggiato dall’Irgun di Menachem Begin, che intendeva riservare alla propria milizia una parte delle armi trasportate. Per Ben Gurion era inaccettabile. Uno Stato, un esercito, uno soltanto. Il seguito è noto. È quel giorno che è stato fondato lo Stato d’Israele. content: By Charles Gardner — A former pop star and model has spoken of her love for Jesus despite being brought up to attend synagogue. One-time Pussycat Dolls member Kaya Jones, whose parents are both Jewish, said: “I wanted to be in the synagogue, and I wanted to have Jesus!” Even as a kid (growing up in America), she felt the two sides – church and synagogue – were part of the same family and needed to be reconciled, quoting the words of Jesus, “I and my Father are one.” (John 10:30) In an interview with Stephen Briggs for his Israel Matters podcast, she said: “I read my Bible and knew that Jesus was my Mashiach (Messiah).” After getting baptised and committing her life to Jesus, she studied at a Hebraic Bible College (which included the New Testament) and has since travelled to Israel to show her support for the beleaguered nation. (photo: KayaJones.com) “The media narrative of Israel is really horrible,” she said. “It’s truly wicked that Israel is having to defend its right to exist.” Referring to the Hamas terrorists as “a death cult”, she echoes the words of her Saviour by saying: “The enemy has come to steal, kill and destroy. But God came to give us life.” (see John 10:10) As for the land, if it is not protected from ongoing threats to wipe out God’s ancient people, will Jesus return there? “God is sending Yeshua (Jesus) back to the exact place [where he ministered on earth],” she said (see Acts 1:11, Zechariah 14:4). “If there is such no place, his arrival will be delayed.” Urging Christians to visit Israel because it turns Bible locations from black and white into technicolour, she said: “It’s not just a storybook or fairytale.” She added that the biggest misconception about Israel is that they are committing genocide, suggesting that this was emphatically not the case. “But there is a war. And if we are going to live in peace, we must listen to what God says in the Torah (the Bible’s section on Law).” The post Former Pussycat Dolls member is Jewish, loves Jesus first appeared on God Reports .

content: By John Pearson — Oh, my. No words, really. JUST READ IT! You must read this extraordinary book, Theo of Golden, a Novel by Allen Levi. This is not a review. No spoiler alerts. Just my obnoxious pleading and begging: you must read this extraordinary book. I know. It’s still November—and I’m announcing my 2026 Book-of-the-Year. (My apologies to the authors of the other 44 books I’ve reviewed so far in 2026, but you’d have to agree with me.) This first-time author, Allen Levi, self-published Theo of Golden in 2023. Word-of-mouth created a publishing sensation and, eventually, a division of Simon & Schuster picked it up. It’s now a New York Times bestseller with more than four million copies sold! If you promise to order the book and read it—you can stop reading my “non-review” right here and move on with your day. If you still need my cajoling…read on. Five notes: #1.  A Gazillion Recommendations Ignored! My apologies to my sister-in-law, Polly Pearson, and dozen of other friends who urged me to read this book. My wife, Joanne, ordered the book last year and she urged (insisted/commanded) that I put aside “all those management books” and read something for fun once in a while. (Finally…mission accomplished. I’m grateful .) #2. Superb Writing. A friend, who is also an author, told me this week he was only eight chapters into the book (60 short chapters, 400 pages)—and he’s given up writing forever! Allen Levi’s wordcrafting…simply superb. #3. I Cheated! Because I borrowed Joanne’s book, with strict instructions not to underline or highlight anything, or make notes in the book, or circle ingenious word combinations ( you know—all the things thoughtful readers do ), I thought, “OK. I’ll just enjoy reading this. I won’t make notes. I won’t read it. I won’t review it.” Oops! I cheated. I couldn’t resist. I made 53 notes on my iPad. I could have made hundreds. I’m not alone. As of this week, Theo of Golden has over 214,000 reviews on Amazon and almost 750,000 ratings on Goodreads. ( It’s #2 on Amazon this week .) #4. He Got Teary-eyed! A pastor texted me—just one-third of the way through the audiobook: “Incredible! Some of the most beautiful writing I’ve ever heard.” While listening on his walk, he got “choked up.” ( Ditto .) #5. Audio, Kindle, or Book? I’m a book guy, but another friend said he was encouraged to listen to the book, while also reading along. I might try that. ( Listen to a three-minute sample here .) The audiobook runs 13 hours and 12 minutes. ( You’ll wish it were longer. Honest .) Allen Levi (YouTube) “Pearson—what’s the book about? I don’t get it. Why won’t you tell me about it?” OK, OK. Here’s the Amazon blurb: “One spring morning, a stranger named Theo arrives in the small Southern city of Golden. He doesn’t explain much about where he came from or why he’s there—but when he visits the local coffeehouse, where pencil portraits of the people of Golden hang on the walls, he begins purchasing them, one at a time, and giving each portrait to the person depicted. In exchange, he asks only for the person’s story. And so portrait by portrait, person by person, secrets are revealed, regrets are shared, and ordinary lives are profoundly altered.” From the back cover: “A story of giving and receiving, of seeing and being seen, Theo of Golden is a beautifully crafted novel about the power of creative generosity, the importance of wonder to a purposeful life, and the invisible threads of kindness that bind us to one another.” “Allen Levi—attorney, judge, singer/songwriter, author—lives on and cares for family acreage near a small town in middle Georgia.” This is his first novel. summary: By Charles Gardner — Getting through life with all its many challenges was particularly tough for Andy Gibson as he was growing up. This was especially the case when his parents separated, and his sister was killed in a car crash. He even prayed and asked God why these things were happening, but heard no […]  The post  Parents’ separation and sisters death turned him from God, Alpha course brought change  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Charles Gardner — Andy Gibson (photo: Gardner) Getting through life with all its many challenges was particularly tough for Andy Gibson as he was growing up. This was especially the case when his parents separated, and his sister was killed in a car crash. He even prayed and asked God why these things were happening, but heard no answers – until much more recently, when a growing relationship with Jesus transformed his life. Now 33, the Doncaster-based railway operations planner has his journey firmly back on track. Having attended a Church of England primary school and subsequently made only occasional visits to church, following Jesus is now the focus of his days. Looking back, he recalls: “I was lost and, moving into my teens, was full of anger, ego and arrogance. I got heavily involved with underage drinking around town and yet, strangely, I’d always pray before going out. “Time moved on and I found myself coasting through life in my twenties – meeting Beth, now my wife, working, saving for a house and having our first child Arlo. “Then in 2019, as the Covid pandemic approached, I was listening to odd things relating to Christianity on YouTube, as a result of which I went to a local church and completed an Alpha course (an introduction to the Christian faith). “In all honesty, it didn’t really interest me. But I gave it a bit of time, feeling that I still wanted to know about Jesus, God and the Bible as a whole. So I went on Google and found BEC (Bessacarr Evangelical Church) which was not far from where we lived. “I remember saying to Beth, ‘I’m going to go there!’ So I went one Sunday evening and was just blown away. The preaching was different to anything I had experienced, and I was finally understanding the Bible. “I couldn’t wait for the following Sunday to find out more. It was like waiting for another episode of a Netflix documentary to come out because we’d be following a specific section of the Bible, studying each chapter in depth as part of a series over several weeks. So I’d be looking forward to an explanation of the next verses the following week. And in due course I publicly declared my faith in Jesus by getting baptised. “Until I started going to church, learning more about the Bible and developing a relationship with Jesus, I never felt fulfilment and love. I never felt I fitted in anywhere until I found Jesus. “I didn’t have answers in my youth. But now I realise it’s not something you can work out all on your own. I can just turn to God’s Word and, through prayer, have a relationship with Jesus. “I can honestly say it’s completely changed every aspect of my life, and I am so grateful that I can’t even put it into words.” Andy and Beth now have a second child, named Red, and are members at BEC, a growing church in a Doncaster suburb. title: From Post-Punk to German Techno—A Musical Journey
summary: By Mark Ellis — Known for his scholarship, journalism, and voice, Brian C. Nixon has another creative life—one that spans more than three decades of songwriting, recording, and musical exploration. Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University, his books, and his journalism for God Reports, ASSIST News Service, and other media […]  The post  From Post-Punk to German Techno—A Musical Journey  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Mark Ellis — Known for his scholarship, journalism, and voice, Brian C. Nixon has another creative life—one that spans more than three decades of songwriting, recording, and musical exploration. Brian Nixon Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University , his books, and his journalism for God Reports , ASSIST News Service , and other media outlets. His voice has also reached listeners across the country through his former involvement with the radio program To Every Man an Answer (later known as Pastors’ Perspective ) and, more recently, Paratus , a program devoted to developing a biblical worldview. What may surprise those familiar with Nixon’s academic and journalistic work is that he is also an accomplished musician and songwriter whose musical journey spans more than 30 years. In his forthcoming book, A Beautiful Defense: How Aesthetics Points to God , co-written with Dr. Patrick Zukeran and scheduled for release in 2027 , Nixon explores the relationship between beauty, faith, and the creative process. In anticipation of the book’s release, I spoke with Nixon about his musical beginnings, his creative influences, and his unexpected venture into German electronic music. Tell me about your early musical journey. I grew up in a musical family. Music was part of my everyday life. During high school, I formed a band with some friends that eventually signed with an independent record label in the San Francisco Bay Area. We released only one record, but several of the other members went on to successful careers in the music industry. One became involved in founding Stones Throw Records, an influential independent label known for its underground hip-hop and experimental music. It was an exciting time. We were young, creative, and discovering what music could be. What did you do after the band broke up? I continued my college education, eventually transferring to California State University, Stanislaus. There, I met another group of musicians, and we formed a band called Canterbury. We ended up winning a Bay Area battle-of-the-bands competition, which was exciting. But rather than continuing in that direction, we decided to pursue something with a more intentional ministry focus. That led to the formation of Widow’s Mite . Widow’s Mite eventually signed with Rick Wakeman, the legendary keyboardist of Yes. Interestingly, that connection also introduced me to journalist Dan Wooding, who wrote Wakeman’s first biography. That relationship eventually opened the door for me to write for ASSIST News Service . So, in a rather unexpected way, my musical career helped launch my journalism career. Widow’s Mite After college, did you continue writing music? Absolutely. I still write music today. My compositions range from jazz and pop to what I call tone poems —short instrumental works that emphasize mood, atmosphere, and musical expression. Some are experimental, while others are much more accessible. I’ve always enjoyed exploring different musical forms rather than staying within a single genre. Interestingly, some of my recent compositions have been selected for rotation by a German online radio station. And here’s the surprising part: they’re German electronic and techno-influenced songs. I’ve been experimenting with AI-assisted production, including using a synthesized female vocalist to interpret my compositions. Did you say German techno? (Laughs.) I know. It sounds funny, doesn’t it? But there’s a story behind it. Recently, I took a deep dive into the music of Kraftwerk, the pioneering German electronic band. I was familiar with their work during high school in the early 1980s because they had influenced so many of the post-punk bands I was listening to at the time. I decided to revisit their entire catalog, and I was blown away all over again. They were years ahead of their time. Their approach to rhythm, synthesizers, repetition, and technology helped shape entire genres of contemporary music.

content: By Charles Gardner — Charles and Linda on their wedding day My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. She just knew that she loved working for them and only left to follow God’s call to work with children. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and Gluckstein dynasty, and the story of how these resilient Jewish families fled violent persecution in Eastern Europe to build what became the largest catering company in the world known as J Lyons & Co. Linda worked there as a home economist from 1977-1984 but it was only much later that she learnt of the Jewish nature of the firm that once literally fed Britain with its teashops and corner houses on every high street, and its products in every home, Linda playing her part through her cooking and marketing skills. A few years later, after graduating from Bible College in Bournemouth, she worked at a prayer and reconciliation centre in Northern Ireland where she was introduced to the importance of the Christian faith’s Jewish roots, as a result of which she took a study tour of Israel to learn more. And on a second trip to the Holy Land ten years later, she got more than she bargained for. At Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, Linda was given a vision of her own wedding. And we met on a blind date six months later! Though having Jewish ancestry myself, I grew up knowing nothing about it. But I learnt more later, especially after becoming a Christian in my early twenties, as Linda had done. It helped that I had a Jewish believer as my early mentor, and I became increasingly aware of the significance of our Jewish heritage, about which I now write prolifically. Meanwhile Linda, who has been teaching Christianity in Doncaster area schools for over 30 years, also now teaches about Judaism as it forms the context into which Christ came to us, fulfilling all the laws and promises of the Old Testament. So in both our cases, we were kept in the dark about very important aspects of our lives – until the Lord shone his light on the truth. Which brings me to the Christian Church as a whole, especially in the UK. We have known very little, if anything, of our faith’s Jewish roots or of God’s ongoing purposes for Israel. This needs to change – and fast! For we are surely hurtling towards the Messiah’s Second Coming like a high-speed train, in danger of coming off the rails with the rest of humanity if we fail to get to grips with how we Christians fit into the unfolding picture of global opposition to tiny Israel. What is our role as we watch antisemitism spread across the globe like wildfire? Do we just sit and watch, or write it off as having nothing to do with us, and remain silent? Or do we stand up to be counted as those who refuse to salute the new Nazism that portrays itself as anti-Zionism – a Confessing Church walking the way of the cross for God’s chosen people? My questions come as renewed calls are made for an independent inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC following news that Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon has won £400,000 in compensation from the broadcaster. Lucie’s career is said to have unravelled after she raised concerns about antisemitism within the BBC, though the latter have not admitted to any fault. This is highly significant as millions of UK Christians are (where Israel is concerned) probably more influenced by what they hear from our national broadcaster than what they read in the Bible. title: New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran
summary: By Howard Cooper — Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the […]  The post  New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Howard Cooper — Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia commons) Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the Senate and the first epidemiologist to serve in the chamber, according to WION News. In an interview with NPR’s Leila Fadel, he said, “I will likely swear on a Quran. Which Quran, we’re not sure.” He pointed to a copy once owned by Thomas Jefferson, which Keith Ellison used when he was sworn in to Congress, and to an old Quran at the University of Michigan that he described as the first in the state. The US Constitution does not require a Bible or any religious text. In practice, senators usually take the formal oath together on the Senate floor, and a Bible comes into play in individual ceremonial swearings-in. El-Sayed hasn’t said whether he’ll use the Quran in the formal proceedings, the ceremony, or both, and that his choice would not alter the wording of the oath. He has also stressed that his oath will be to the U.S. Constitution,  according to IBTimes. He will be sworn in by Vice President JD Vance, a fact El-Sayed has noted with humor. The Blaze reported he called it a “delicious irony” that Vance is constitutionally required to do so. Not everyone is comfortable with the news. The Daily Signal reported that former White House press secretary Sean Spicer said this week that given El-Sayed’s connections and statements, he should undergo a formal background check before receiving classified information. Presumably, Spicer was referring to Al-Sayed’s family connections to the Muslim Brotherhood. For many Christians, the moment raises questions about the role of faith in public life, the long American tradition of religious liberty, and the Judeo-Christian roots of the United States. El-Sayed and his colleagues are scheduled to be sworn in at noon on January 3, 2027. The post New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran first appeared on God Reports .

content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. title: Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin
summary: By Mark Ellis — Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, […]  The post  Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

content: By Brian Nixon — The word epiphany is defined by the Oxford Learner’s Dictionary as “a sudden and surprising moment of understanding.” Often, such epiphany moments arrive unexpectedly, interrupting the ordinary rhythms of life with extraordinary insight. Sometimes they come through a conversation, a passage of Scripture, or an encounter with nature. Other times, they emerge through art. Twilight Epiphany. Photo: Eliott Davis Sitting beneath artist James Turrell’s Twilight Epiphany on the campus of Rice University in Houston, Texas, on a Sunday morning as the sun rose, the word epiphany took on new meaning. As the morning light slowly illuminated the sky, subtle shifts in color transformed the space above me. The experience was both architectural and atmospheric, a convergence of art, nature, and contemplation. Turrell, born in 1943, is an American artist internationally recognized for his exploration of light, space, and human perception. Raised in the Quaker tradition, Turrell’s artistic vision reflects an appreciation for silence, stillness, and inward reflection. Commissioned by Rice University through the generosity of alumna Suzanne Deal Booth, Twilight Epiphany opened in 2012 as part of the university’s public art program. The pyramidal Skyspace, designed to accommodate approximately 120 visitors, features an aperture in its roof through which viewers observe the changing sky. At sunrise and sunset, carefully programmed LED lights interact with the natural atmosphere, creating an extraordinary experience of shifting color and perception. More than a work of architecture, the installation invites visitors to slow down, look upward, and reconsider the relationship between light and the world around them. James Turrell (Chat GPT) For me, the experience was something of a spiritual exercise. Light, after all, is among the Bible’s most enduring metaphors for divine revelation, truth, and beauty. As the colors shifted above me, I was reminded that beauty does not always announce itself loudly. Sometimes it simply asks us to be still and pay attention. Rothko Chapel. Photo: https://www.mark-rothko.org/rothko-chapel.jsp#google_vignette. From Rice University, I headed to another meditative landmark: the Rothko Chapel . Here, I sat among the monumental, dark-hued paintings of Mark Rothko, contemplating both the tragedy of the artist’s life and the triumph of the chapel that bears his name. Commissioned by Houston philanthropists John and Dominique de Menil in 1964 and dedicated in 1971, the Rothko Chapel is an interfaith sanctuary devoted to contemplation, spiritual reflection, and human rights. Its octagonal interior contains fourteen large-scale paintings by Rothko, whose subtle variations of black, maroon, and purple create an atmosphere of profound stillness. Rothko, born Marcus Rothkowitz in 1903, was a leading figure in American Abstract Expressionism, celebrated for his ability to evoke deep emotional responses through color and form. Yet his personal life was marked by physical illness, depression, and emotional turmoil. In February 1970, before the chapel’s dedication, Rothko died by suicide at the age of sixty-six. He never witnessed the completed sanctuary that would become one of his most enduring artistic legacies. Twilight Epiphany. Photo: Brian C. Nixon There is something deeply moving about this juxtaposition. An artist whose life ended in despair left behind a place where countless visitors have sought peace, meaning, and solace. The darkness of Rothko’s paintings does not necessarily communicate hopelessness. Rather, their quiet intensity invites viewers to confront the depths of human experience—sorrow, longing, mystery, and perhaps even transcendence. Where Turrell’s Twilight Epiphany draws the eyes upward toward the heavens, Rothko’s chapel seems to draw the gaze inward, toward the mysteries of the human soul. One is animated by the changing light of the sky, the other by the stillness of darkened canvases. Ye

title: Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success
summary: By Brian Nixon — While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: John Warwick Montgomery By Brian Nixon — While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. summary: What do Jesus and Isaiah have in common? Quite a bit, according to renowned British New Testament scholar N. T. Wright.
